idiom_name: hand-written function-pointer-table fake with a bounded operation journal
implementation_notes: C has no interfaces, so the collaborator is a struct of function pointers and the recording fake is a hand-written implementation of that table whose callbacks update an in-memory store and append a typed entry to a journal array owned by the fake; nothing in the standard library replaces this compound. cmocka and CMock generate mock objects with queued expectations, not working recorders, so a behaving double that also records still has to be written by hand. Keep the journal behind accessor functions that only tests call, pass the table plus its context into the module under test instead of letting it call the real functions, and reset the fake per test case.
pitfalls: File-scope or static fake state (the store and the journal) is shared by every test in the binary - allocate the fake per case or reset it in setup.
A function-pointer table is not checked across translation units: a signature drift compiles and corrupts the stack at runtime, so declare the table once in a header.
Fixed-capacity journals and manual ownership are unmanaged: an overflowing array or a journal freed while the module still holds the fake is undefined behaviour - bound the log or fail loudly.
